source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.5.1, opening words 'for each p >= 1' and 'X ~ N(0, 1)'
source_evidence.observation: The enclosing exercise fixes a standard normal random variable and considers its absolute moments for exponents p at least 1.
The source explicitly identifies the L^p norm as ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) and gives an exact Gamma-function expression before asking for the asymptotic deduction.
The numbered claim is ||X||_{L^p} = O(sqrt(p)) as p tends to infinity.

The source describes (2.11) as the growth of moments and, in the ensuing general sub-gaussian property, expresses that growth by an upper bound ||X||_{L^p} <= K_2 sqrt(p) for all p >= 1. This is surrounding interpretive context, not an additional clause of the numbered equation.

binders: X is a random variable with the standard normal distribution N(0,1) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Exercise 2.5.1).
p is an exponent satisfying p >= 1 in the enclosing exercise, with (2.11) concerning the regime p -> infinity (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Exercise 2.5.1 and display (2.11)).
hypotheses: X ~ N(0,1) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Exercise 2.5.1).
The L^p absolute moment is considered for p >= 1 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, opening of Exercise 2.5.1).
conclusions: As p -> infinity, ||X||_{L^p} = O(sqrt(p)) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, display (2.11)).

Thus (2.11) asserts an asymptotic upper growth bound of square-root order; it does not itself state a matching lower bound or asymptotic equivalence (PDF page 13; printed page 24, the one-sided big-O notation in display (2.11)).
definitions_and_conventions: The enclosing exercise explicitly writes ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, displayed equality before (2.11)).

The standard asymptotic reading of O(sqrt(p)) as p -> infinity is that there are constants C > 0 and p_0 such that ||X||_{L^p} <= C sqrt(p) whenever p >= p_0; the source does not define big-O locally, while Proposition 2.5.2(ii) immediately afterward confirms the intended upper-bound form (PDF page 13; printed page 24, display (2.11) and Proposition 2.5.2(ii)).

The exact Gamma-function identity immediately before (2.11) is supporting context from which the exercise asks the reader to deduce the numbered asymptotic statement; it is not itself labeled (2.11) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Exercise 2.5.1).

The quantity is the L^p norm defined from the p-th absolute moment, ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, equality before (2.11)).

Only O(sqrt(p)) is displayed: no lower bound, Theta statement, or limit for ||X||_{L^p}/sqrt(p) is part of (2.11) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, display (2.11)).

contract_plain_english: For a standard normal random variable X, its L^p norm—defined here as (E|X|^p)^(1/p)—grows no faster than a constant times sqrt(p) as p tends to infinity. Equation (2.11) is only this upper asymptotic growth assertion. The exact Gamma-function formula immediately before it explains why the bound holds but is not itself part of the numbered equation.
